respuesta.pregunta: I'm trying to run catalog-portfolio-api locally and keep hitting two problems: the port is already in use when the service starts, and the Gradle build is acting up. What's the recommended fix for each?
respuesta.respuesta:
Both documented versions, 0.0.1-test-bench-v2a and latest, have the same local-development troubleshooting guidance, so the fixes below hold for either one.

- **Port already in use:** You can change the port in `application.properties`, or you can kill the process that's holding it with `lsof -ti:8080 | xargs kill -9` [catalog-portfolio-api/0.0.1-test-bench-v2a/guide/setup/local-development.md:L123-L127] [catalog-portfolio-api/latest/guide/setup/local-development.md:L123-L127].
- **Gradle build issues:** Do a clean rebuild. Run `./gradlew clean`, then `./gradlew build --refresh-dependencies` [catalog-portfolio-api/0.0.1-test-bench-v2a/guide/setup/local-development.md:L129-L135] [catalog-portfolio-api/latest/guide/setup/local-development.md:L129-L135].

The same section also lists some commands that can help you figure out what's going on:
- `jps -v` shows the Java processes that are running.
- `tail -f logs/application.log` follows the application log.
[catalog-portfolio-api/0.0.1-test-bench-v2a/guide/setup/local-development.md:L139-L148] [catalog-portfolio-api/latest/guide/setup/local-development.md:L139-L148]
